name: Interim valuations, payment notices, retention and the final account
one_line: The organizational situation of money AS THE CONTRACT SEES IT: a construction contract pays in a repeating cycle - the party doing the work applies for a cumulative valuation, the other side issues a notice or a certificate saying what it considers due, retention is withheld against future release, and at the end the whole thing is reconciled into a single agreed final account of additions and omissions. The organizing anchor is the CONTRACT and its numbered valuation cycle, not a supplier and not a ledger period, which is why this is a different situation from bookkeeping even though every document in it carries a total. Absorbs the legacy row cons.final-account (ROW) - the interim cycle and the closing settlement are one continuous account and cannot be filed apart from each other. Gist-level placeholder (J-IND): it recognizes the situation and writes NO field rows, because the construction_property schema declares none.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every entry below is a DETECTION signal, never an extraction licence - this template's schema declares no field rows (PR-6; D1's deferral stands). “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

an application-for-payment structure: a numbered valuation or application, a valuation date, a GROSS cumulative valuation, a line deducting the amount previously certified, a retention deduction expressed as a percentage of the gross, and a net amount now due. The cumulative-minus-previously-certified arithmetic is the discriminating shape - an ordinary invoice states one period's charge and never subtracts what it billed last month. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”

a payment-notice structure: a notice naming the sum the issuer considers due and the basis on which that sum was calculated, dated against a payment cycle - a due date and a final date for payment - rather than against ordinary invoice payment terms.

a pay-less or withholding notice: the same contract and valuation reference, a LOWER sum than the one applied for, and reasons for the deduction. It exists only in answer to a specific application, which makes the pair a structural unit.

a certificate structure: an interim or final certificate signed by a named contract administrator, quantity surveyor, architect or employer's agent, CERTIFYING a sum owed by one party to another rather than demanding a sum for the signer's own account.

a retention statement: a running account of amounts withheld with a two-stage release - part at practical completion, the balance at the end of the defects period. A two-stage release schedule appears nowhere else in this product's corpus.

a final-account structure: an original contract sum, a schedule of ADDITIONS AND OMISSIONS (variations, provisional-sum adjustments, loss and expense, fluctuations), an adjusted total, and wording to the effect that the account is agreed in full and final settlement.
a measured-works build-up whose line items are priced against a bill of quantities or a schedule of rates and carry a percentage-complete or quantity-to-date column.
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: any model step runs after P7 and under the user's policy, and must abstain rather than guess: “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”

which side of the payment cycle the file sits on. The same valuation exists in the payer's file as a certificate and in the payee's as an application, with substantially identical numbers; only purpose separates them. “Topic answers what a file is about, while purpose answers what the file was for.”
separating a draft final account still under negotiation from the agreed one, when both are spreadsheets with identical tabs, no version token in the filename, and different totals.
deciding whether an unlabeled spreadsheet of additions and omissions is a final account, a variation register, or an internal cost report - three different situations with the same columns.
recognising that a settlement letter or an email exchange, not any document called an account, is the operative agreement that closed the account.
a photographed day-work sheet that has been priced up in the same image - part timesheet, part valuation substantiation.

a valuation pack whose members are individually unremarkable - a summary, a measure, a variation schedule, photographs and a delay narrative - and coherent only by purpose. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
never_alone: a money total, a currency token or a percentage alone. Retention reads as a percentage; so does VAT, so does a discount, so does a completion figure. This is the single most tempting false signal in the row.

an invoice header alone. A demand for payment with an invoice number and payment terms is a bookkeeping transaction even when a construction firm issued it - this is the collision fixture, and finance.small-business-bookkeeping owns it.
the word final in a filename alone - it is the most overloaded version token in any corpus and says nothing about a contract account.

a client's, employer's or contractor's organisation name alone, read across by inference from “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.”
a bare 4-digit number, which here is as likely to be a valuation number, a drawing number, a contract number or a rate as a year.

membership in a download session that pulled a whole valuation pack from a portal at once - “A session should never be treated as proof of topic, and it should not carry the same confidence as a hash match or a directly extracted document fact.”

an extension or a source_type alone - “The engine should treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning, inspect the real MIME type or file signature where possible, and dispatch each file to a type-specific extractor.”

grouping_reasons: one valuation cycle: the application, the payment notice, any pay-less notice, the certificate and the remittance, held together by a valuation reference and a date. The pay-less notice and the application it answers must never be separated - the pair is the evidence, not either half.
one contract's whole valuation series read as a running account, because each valuation is meaningless without the one before it: the arithmetic is cumulative by construction.
one final account across its drafts, which is a version family before it is anything else, and where the differences between drafts are the negotiation.
a valuation and the substantiation attached to it - measures, day-work sheets, photographs, variation instructions - purpose-coherent and content-incoherent.
no group at all is a valid outcome: a single remittance advice, or one certificate that arrived alone, is a standalone record.

template.why: Empty by binding contract: construction_property declares no field rows (J-IND / PR-6, D1's deferral as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15), so no dimension can branch - a dimension naming an undeclared field opens a tree level no fact could ever fill. Held as prose for the pass that may license fields: the natural anchor is the CONTRACT or project, then the payment stage - interim cycle versus final account - then, inside the interim cycle only, the numbered valuation. The valuation number must sit under the contract and not above it, because valuation 07 identifies nothing on its own and every contract has one. “The recommendation should follow the practical rule that a parent dimension should provide the context required to understand the child.” Not time-first, even though the cycle is periodic: “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” - a monthly-folder tree would scatter one contract's running account across two or three calendar years and break exactly the continuity that makes the arithmetic checkable. Privacy caveat specific to this row: a valuation build-up discloses margin, preliminaries and often a subcontractor's own rates, a retention or pay-less dispute is an allegation about a named counterparty's performance, and a final account states what a business was actually worth on one job - none of which should acquire automatic internal depth or reach a model prompt by default. The user may reverse, remove or flatten any of this later; this is a recommendation, not a frozen filesystem.

collides_with.signal: The sharpest collision in the row: every valuation eventually becomes an invoice and a ledger entry, and the same client, the same works and the same total appear on both. The discriminating evidence: cumulative arithmetic - a gross valuation less previously certified less retention - together with a contract payment cycle supports this row; an invoice number, tax treatment, payment terms and a posting or nominal reference supports bookkeeping. A total alone discriminates neither.

Variations are priced INSIDE a final account, so a schedule of additions and omissions appears in both files. The discriminating evidence: an instruction number with a narrative of entitlement, a contractual clause cited and a cause-and-effect argument supports the variation row; the reconciliation of the whole contract sum with amounts already certified supports this row.

Payment applications and payment notices run down the chain in exactly the same form, so the firm's own application to its client and its subcontractor's application to it are structurally identical documents. The discriminating evidence: which agreement the reference names - a subcontract or order reference with the firm as payer supports the subcontract row; the main contract reference with the firm as payee supports this row. A valuation number alone discriminates neither.

The project row is the container that gives a valuation its meaning, and a project folder holds valuations among everything else. The discriminating evidence: the payment cycle apparatus - applications, notices, certificates, retention - supports this row; award documents, programmes, instructions, correspondence and the general project record support the project row.

A priced schedule of measured works looks the same before and after the work is done. The discriminating evidence: a validity period, an acceptance line and no reference to work already carried out supports the quote row; a percentage-complete or quantity-to-date column and a deduction of what was previously certified supports this row.

Day-work sheets are labour records that become valuation substantiation once priced. The discriminating evidence: rates, a valuation reference and a claimed sum supports this row; hours, names and a payroll or allocation purpose supports the timesheet row.

Both sit on an executed contract and cite the same clauses. The discriminating evidence: an obligations register, notice periods, renewal dates and the management of the agreement supports contract administration; the periodic movement of money under the agreement supports this row.

Reciprocal to that row's own construction collision: a bill of quantities and a pricing schedule are shared shapes. The discriminating evidence: a solicitation reference, a submission deadline and competing responses supports the sourcing row; payment under an awarded contract supports this row.

falls_through_to.why: The home for a standalone certificate, notice or settlement letter with no accepted contract group around it. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

The correct home for the transactional side this row must not absorb - an isolated invoice or a remittance advice. “Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.”

The cautious outcome for an unlabeled schedule of additions and omissions, or a draft account whose status is unresolved. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

The safe outcome for a password-protected valuation pack or an unreadable portal export, both routine where certification runs through a client's payment portal. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

sensitivity_why: A valuation build-up discloses what a business actually costs and earns - preliminaries, margin, and frequently a subcontractor's own rates held in confidence. A pay-less notice is a written allegation of defective or incomplete work against a named counterparty, and day-work substantiation names individual workers and their hours. 00 names the corpus this product handles - it “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records.” - and account statements and employment materials of this kind fall inside it. The operative limits are 00's: “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.” This row assigns only the catalogue value potentially_sensitive; it does not assign, alias, rank, or infer a P7 handling class.
open_question: Where the seam between this row and finance.small-business-bookkeeping should fall for a small trade business, where applying for payment and issuing the invoice are one act performed once a month. For a main contractor the two are unmistakably different systems; for a two-person firm the valuation IS the invoice, and forcing them apart would split one monthly folder in half. This row keeps the contractual cycle because the roster hint says money as the contract sees it, before accounting sees it - but the point at which a job becomes small enough for that distinction to be noise is a real user-specific line and it is Joseph's to draw. A second, narrower question: whether the closing final account deserves its own row separate from the interim cycle it settles. This row says no, because the account is arithmetically continuous with the valuations - but a quantity surveyor would file them apart.
